title: Detect Squares
spaceBreakdown:
- unordered_map<int, unordered_map<int,int>> cnt: up to D distinct points → O(D)
- recursion depth: none
- not counted: input, returned int
approach: Store point frequencies in a nested hash map (x → y → count). For a query point (x, y), iterate over every stored point (px, py) as the potential opposite (diagonal) corner. The other two corners are then (x, py) and (px, y); look up their frequencies and multiply all three. Only count when |px−x| = |py−y| (square, not rectangle) and px ≠ x, py ≠ y (positive area). Each valid square has exactly one diagonal pair involving the query point, so no double-counting.
hints: Given the query point as one corner of an axis-aligned square, which other single corner of the square would let you determine the positions of all remaining corners?
Use a nested hash map (x → y → frequency). For query (11, 10), the stored point (3, 2) is the opposite corner; the other two corners (11, 2) and (3, 10) are looked up in the map.

```
for each stored point (px, py) with px ≠ x and py ≠ y:
    if |px - x| ≠ |py - y|: skip
    ans += freq(px, py) × freq(x, py) × freq(px, y)
return ans
```

**Query point also stored** - the query point may itself be in the data structure
`add [11, 10], add [3, 10], add [11, 2], add [3, 2], count [11, 10]` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: not skipping px == x → counts (11, 10) as its own diagonal, returns 2

**Duplicate points** - the same point added multiple times multiplies valid square counts
`add [3, 10], add [11, 2], add [3, 2], add [11, 2], count [11, 10]` → `Expected: 2`
⚠️ Bug: using a set instead of a frequency map → returns 1

**Rectangle, not square** - four points form an axis-aligned rectangle with unequal sides
`add [1, 1], add [5, 3], add [1, 3], add [5, 1], count [1, 1]` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: not checking |px - x| == |py - y| → counts the rectangle, returns 1

**Multiple valid squares** - two different diagonals each form a valid square
`add [1, 1], add [3, 3], add [1, 3], add [3, 1], add [5, 5], add [5, 1], add [1, 5], count [1, 1]` → `Expected: 2`
⚠️ Bug: breaking after the first valid diagonal → returns 1

followUps.q: What if coordinates can be up to 10^9 instead of 1000?
followUps.a: The nested hash map approach already handles arbitrary coordinate values, so no change is needed. Time and space complexity remain O(D) per count and O(D) total.

followUps.q: What if we also need to support removing a point?
followUps.a: Add a remove method that decrements the frequency and erases the inner entry when it reaches zero. Count logic stays identical. Time per remove is O(1) amortized.

followUps.q: What if the query asks for axis-aligned rectangles (any aspect ratio) instead of squares?
followUps.a: Remove the |px - x| == |py - y| check. Every stored point (px, py) with px ≠ x and py ≠ y becomes a valid diagonal. Time complexity stays O(D) per count.
